#firewall

What one machine listens on and what its firewall, ufw, lets through, for a web page. First the ports, each with how far its address reaches and what the firewall does to it, Allow or Close from its row; then ufw's rules, on or off, its defaults, a row to add one, and × to delete one with Undo. A change shows at once, marked while the machine makes it.

It has two halves and knows nothing of where the machine is. The page half is a Vue component that talks to an HTTP API under one base URL. The server half is that API, as one request handler that asks the host for two things: to run ufw with a list of words, as root, on the machine, and for the ports it listens on. The host gives those, mounts the handler at the base, and decides who may ask.

serviceman is the first host: its Remote page has a Firewall tab (which took in the Ports tab there was), ufw runs in the machine's root half, or with sudo -n where it has none, and the ports are the list its agent reads with ss.

#Layout

server/firewall_serve.js      the HTTP API, given run(argv) and ports()
ui/firewall.js                the component
ui/firewall_ports.js          the ports as rows: how far each reaches, what the firewall does
ui/firewall.css               the component's rules
tests/firewall_serve.test.js  the API over a fake ufw, or a real one (below)
tests/firewall_ports.test.js  what each kind of port and rule comes to
tests/fake_ufw.js             ufw as far as the module asks it, saying what ufw 0.36 says

#The rules are the ones ufw lists as added

ufw status lists no rules while the firewall is off, and every rule twice (v4 and v6) while it is on. The module reads ufw show added instead: one line a rule, each the command that made it, the same on as off. So a rule is deleted by what it is (ufw delete allow 22/tcp), never by a number that moves under it, and Undo is the same command again, at its old place (ufw insert <n> …), since the first rule that matches is the one ufw goes by.

#The API

Under the base the host mounts it at — serviceman's is /api/v1/remotes/<name>/firewall. Every answer about the firewall that succeeds is the firewall as it is now:

{installed, active, defaults: {incoming, outgoing, routed} or null while off, logging,
 ssh_open, rules: [{command, action, direction, port, proto, from, to, on, app, comment}]}
Door What it does
GET <base> the firewall; installed: false on a machine without ufw
GET <base>/ports what the host's ports() answers: {items: [{proto, address, port, state, users: [{name, pid}]}], commands}; 501 without one
POST <base>/rules {action, direction, port, proto, from, comment} a rule from the form, added last
POST <base>/rules {command, at} a rule as the list gave it, put back at its place: Undo
POST <base>/rules/delete {command} one rule of the list gone; answers undo: {command, at}
POST <base>/enable on (ufw --force enable: ufw's question about ssh answered ahead)
POST <base>/disable off; the rules are kept
  • The form: action is allow, deny, reject or limit; direction in or out; port a number, a range (8000:8100) or a list (80,443); proto tcp, udp or any (a range or a list needs one of the first two); from an address or a network, empty for anywhere; comment one line, no '. It is checked before ufw is asked: a 400 says what is wrong.
  • ssh_open says whether a rule lets ssh (22) in; the page warns before the firewall is turned on without one.
  • Refusals: a rule ufw has already, or one that is gone from the list since the page read it, is a 409. ufw that cannot be run, or a sudo that wants a password, is a 502 that says so.

#What a port comes to

ui/firewall_ports.js makes the rows the page shows, from the ports, the machine's own addresses and the firewall:

  • One row per port and holder: v4 and v6 of one program are one row, as exposed as the most exposed of its addresses; the most exposed come first.
  • How far its address reaches: the internet (a public address, or every address of a machine that has a public one), a network (private, link-local, the tailnet's 100.64.0.0/10, a multicast group or a broadcast), or this machine only (loopback).
  • What the firewall does: the first rule for the port (its protocol or both, the port in its list or range, a rule for every port, ssh by name for 22) that holds for everyone decides, as ufw goes by the first match; rules for one source are said beside it; with none, the default (deny while ufw is off, since its status does not say). While the firewall is off the row says what it will be once on.
  • Close is offered only where the rule that lets a port in is about that port alone; a range, a service by name or the default is changed in the rules.

#Plugging it into a host

const firewall_serve = require('../modules/firewall/server/firewall_serve');

// every request under /firewall goes to the module; the host checks who may ask first
await firewall_serve(req, res, {
    run: argv => run_as_root(['ufw'].concat(argv)),    // -> {ok, code, stdout, stderr}
    ports: () => listening_ports(),                     // -> {items, commands}
    tail: '/rules',                                     // the address after the base
    log: function (event, fields) {
    },
});

The page half: the host serves ui/ and maps it in its import map:

<link rel="stylesheet" href="/modules/firewall/firewall.css">
{"imports": {"firewall/": "/modules/firewall/", "vue": "/vendor/vue.esm-browser.prod.js"}}

import firewall from 'firewall/firewall.js';

<firewall base="/firewall" :offline="false" :addresses="['203.0.113.7']"/>

addresses are the machine's own, for how far a port on every address reaches; without them such a port is taken for open to the internet. stays is what still reaches the machine once the firewall closes ssh, said after the warning that it will (serviceman's agent dials out).

The host page gives the colours, as --panel, --line, --muted, --fg and --accent, and the classes the component shares with it: card, list-head, list-acts, list-table, dot, muted, bad, primary, link, pill, chip, and --run, --busy, --bad for the colours of open, warned and kept out.

#In serviceman

  • src/main/src/routes/handle_control_request.js sends /api/v1/remotes/<name>/firewall… to firewall_serve, after its own refusals: no such machine, not connected, an agent from before the firewall; its ports() is the agent's port_list, asked of the root half where there is one so every holder is named
  • the agent's ufw call (src/agent/src/agent_ufw.js) runs ufw with the words given, only its own subcommands (status, show, allow, deny, reject, limit, delete, insert, enable, disable), with no shell between: in the root half where the machine has one, else as sudo -n ufw, so a sudoers line may name ufw and nothing else; --ufw (SERVICEMAN_UFW) names another ufw; a root half older than this says it is updating rather than falling back to sudo
  • src/main/public/remote_firewall.js is the Firewall tab, which wraps the component and gives it the machine's addresses; an old /remotes/<name>/ports address opens it

#Tests

node --test modules/firewall/tests/*.test.js

Against a real ufw, which they reset: as root, in a container that may change its firewall,

podman run --rm --cap-add NET_ADMIN --cap-add NET_RAW -e UFW=ufw -v $PWD:/app:ro alpine \
    sh -c 'apk add ufw nodejs && node --test /app/modules/firewall/tests/firewall_serve.test.js'
